paper_metadata.title: A Stabilization Technique for Phase-Locked Frequency Synthesizers
paper_metadata.abstract: A stabilization technique is presented that relaxes the tradeoff between the settling speed and the magnitude of output sidebands in phase-locked frequency synthesizers. The method introduces a zero in the open-loop transfer function through the use of a discrete-time delay cell, obviating the need for resistors in the loop filter. A 2.4-GHz CMOS frequency synthesizer employing the technique settles in approximately 60 s with 1-MHz channel spacing while exhibiting a sideband magnitude of 58.7 dBc. Designed for Bluetooth applications and fabricated in a 0.25m digital CMOS technology, the synthesizer achieves a phase noise of 112 dBc/Hz at 1-MHz offset and consumes 20 mW from a 2.5-V supply.
